newsitem.title: USA: Dow crosses 8,000 mark for first time, then eases.
newsitem.headline: Dow crosses 8,000 mark for first time, then eases.

text.p: The Dow Jones Industrial average pushed across the 8,000 level for the first time ever on Wednesday morning, then quickly retreated as shares of component Eastman Kodak Co opened lower.

The Dow tacked on a speedy 24 points, hitting 8,000. But it quickly eased, shedding around 21 points to trade at 7955 when Kodak's stock opened down 9-3/8 at 67-1/2 after the company posted below-forecast results.
Kodak reported second quarter earnings of $1.12 per share compared with $1.30 in the year-ago quarter and a First Call consensus estimate of $1.39 per share.
While the Dow slid, the Nasdaq composite continued to post powerful gains, rising 16 points, or 1.02 percent, to 1558.
Nasdaq was propelled by strength in chipmaker Intel Corp, whose better-than-expected second quarter results also inspired other technology stocks.
Intel reported second quarter earnings of $0.92 per share compared with $0.59 per share in the year-ago second quarter and a First Call estimate of $0.90 per share.
The long bond added support, rising 12/32 to yield 6.52 percent after a benign consumer price report for June.
